slides.text: The same technology that helps a kid finish a homework assignment is being used to clone a grandmother's voice. We have to teach both sides.

slides.title: What's New About AI Scams
bullets: Fake voices that sound like your real family members
Texts and emails written in perfect, polite English
Fake websites that look exactly like real banks
AI calls that pass for a real customer service rep
Scammers use AI to scale faster than ever before
slides.note: Many seniors think 'I would notice.' Show real examples to make the threat concrete.

slides.title: Red Flags to Watch For
bullets: Urgency: 'You need to act right now or else'
Unusual payment methods: gift cards, wire, crypto
Strange greetings: 'Dear customer' from your own bank
A familiar voice asking for money or passwords
Anything you'd be embarrassed to ask family about

slides.title: Seeing Isn't Believing Anymore
bullets: Photos and videos can be faked with one click
AI can clone a voice from 3 seconds of audio
Fake news articles look like real ones
Even live video calls can be manipulated
Always verify shocking content from a second source

slides.title: Hands-On: Spot the Fake
steps: Look at the four photos on the screen
Two are real, two are AI-generated
Discuss with your neighbor which is which
We'll reveal the answers together
Notice what gave the fakes away — and what didn't

slides.title: Your Data Is the Product
bullets: Most free apps make money from your information
Don't paste sensitive details into any AI tool
Never share Social Security or banking info with AI
Use strong, unique passwords for every account
Turn on two-factor authentication everywhere you can

slides.title: Use AI Without Getting Burned
bullets: Read what data the tool collects before you sign up
Don't share private health, legal, or financial info
Verify any factual claim from a second source
Treat AI like a smart but unreliable assistant
When in doubt, ask a real person you trust

slides.title: Module 5: When NOT to Trust AI
Hard Lines
bullets: Medical decisions — always confirm with a doctor
Legal decisions — always confirm with a lawyer
Anything involving money or passwords
Voting and election information — go to the source
Anything that sounds emotionally urgent
slides.note: Plant the flag here: AI helps with information, humans make decisions.

slides.title: Hands-On: The Grandparent Scam Drill
steps: We'll play a 30-second AI-cloned voice clip
Pretend it's a panicked call from a grandchild
Write down: what would you do first?
We'll discuss the safe answer (verify by calling them)
Practice this with your real family this week

slides.title: What You Walk Away With
bullets: Knowing the top scam patterns to watch for
A safety checklist to take home
A family verification phrase to use when calls feel off
Confidence to ask 'is this real?' without embarrassment
A SCAiL contact for follow-up questions

sc-6.title: Youth AI Lab: Build Your First AI Project

slides.title: Youth AI Lab
slides.subtitle: Build Your First AI Project — In 6 Weeks

slides.title: Six Weeks, One Project
items: Week 6: Demo Day — show what you built

slides.text: You're already smarter than the AI in some ways. The trick is figuring out which ways — and using AI for the rest.

slides.title: What AI Actually Is
bullets: AI learns from millions of examples
It guesses the most likely next word, image, or answer
It is built by people who chose what to feed it
Those choices shape what it can and can't do
Understanding this is your superpower

slides.title: The Ethics Conversation
bullets: Whose work was AI trained on? Did they get paid?
Who is harmed when AI is wrong about people?
Is using AI for school work cheating? When? Why?
What jobs might disappear? What jobs might appear?
These are YOUR questions — the answers aren't decided yet
slides.note: Don't lecture. Open it up. The students will surprise you.

slides.title: Better Prompts, Better Results
bullets: Be specific about what you want
Tell AI who it should be (a tutor, a coach, a friend)
Show examples of the kind of answer you want
Ask follow-up questions instead of starting over
If the answer is bad, the prompt is usually the problem

slides.title: Hands-On: Prompt Race
steps: Pair up with a partner
Goal: Get ChatGPT to write a 4-line poem about Columbia, SC
Round 1: Use a one-line prompt
Round 2: Use a 5-line, specific prompt
Compare and discuss what changed

slides.title: Build Without Coding
bullets: Bolt.new — turn an idea into a website by talking
Replit — build apps with AI as your co-pilot
Glide — turn a Google Sheet into a real app
Canva AI — design like a pro in minutes
All free or have free tiers for students

slides.title: Your First Real AI Build
bullets: Pick a problem in your school or community
Design a chatbot that helps with that problem
Use a no-code tool to actually build it
Test it with a real person
Iterate based on what they tell you

slides.title: Hands-On: Build the First Version
steps: Open Bolt.new on your laptop
Tell it what your chatbot should do, in plain English
Watch it build the first version in front of you
Click through it. Find what's broken.
Tell Bolt what to fix — and watch it fix it

slides.title: Make Things You Couldn't Make Before
bullets: Generate art, music, and video clips
Write a short story with AI as your editor
Build a game level using AI tools
Make a real video for your social media
Use AI to amplify your creativity, not replace it

slides.title: Show Your Work
bullets: 3-minute demo of what you built
Share what worked and what broke
Explain the problem you solved
Take questions from the room
Trade tips with the other builders

slides.title: What This Means for Your Future
bullets: A real project for college applications
A portfolio piece that didn't exist 3 years ago
Skills employers actively hire for in 2026
Confidence to keep building on your own
A network of fellow young SCAiL builders

slides.title: What You Walk Away With
bullets: An AI project you built and demoed
Real prompt engineering skills
Working knowledge of 4+ no-code AI tools
A portfolio piece for college and jobs
A SCAiL Youth Lab credential — first cohort in SC

slides.title: AI Leadership Academy
slides.subtitle: Lead AI Adoption in Your Organization

slides.text: The organizations that win the next decade won't be the ones with the most AI. They'll be the ones whose people understand it best.

slides.title: Strategy Before Tools
bullets: Don't start with 'which AI tool should we buy?'
Start with 'what are we actually trying to do better?'
Map your top 5 organizational pain points
Match AI capabilities to those pain points
Pick ONE pilot — small, measurable, reversible
slides.note: This is the most common mistake leaders make. Repeat it twice.

slides.title: The 3-Question Framework
bullets: Where are we losing the most time today?
Where are we making the most preventable errors?
Where could AI help us reach more people for less money?
Pick the answer that overlaps all three
That's where your AI pilot starts

slides.title: Leading Through Change
bullets: Most people fear AI because they fear losing their jobs
Acknowledge that fear directly — never dismiss it
Frame AI as a tool that elevates people, not replaces them
Train your team early — anxiety drops with familiarity
Celebrate early wins publicly

slides.title: What 'AI-Powered' Actually Looks Like
bullets: AI integrated into your weekly workflow, not bolted on
Every staff member has at least one AI use case
Decisions are still made by humans, faster
Routine tasks are automated, freeing time for relationships
Your impact per dollar goes up — measurably

slides.title: AI for Grant Writing
bullets: Use AI to research funders that match your mission
Draft first versions of LOIs and proposals 10x faster
Use AI to summarize past funder reports
Personalize outreach emails to major donors
Always edit and verify — AI is a draft engine, not a sender

slides.title: Hands-On: Grant Research Sprint
steps: Open ChatGPT on your laptop
Describe your organization's mission in 3 sentences
Ask: 'List 10 funders that match this mission'
Verify each one online — at least 3 should be real
Save the verified list — that's your prospect pipeline

slides.title: AI Governance for Your Organization
bullets: Write a one-page AI use policy for your staff
Define what data can and cannot be put into AI tools
Be transparent with stakeholders about your AI use
Audit AI outputs regularly for bias and errors
Treat AI ethics as a competitive advantage, not a constraint

slides.title: Hard Questions to Sit With
bullets: Whose voice could be flattened by AI in your work?
What relationships could AI accidentally damage?
What's your plan when AI is confidently wrong?
How do you train your team to recognize bias?
How will you tell your community about your AI use?

slides.title: Your Capstone Project
bullets: A written AI implementation plan for your organization
A pitch deck for your board or funders
A 90-day roadmap with measurable milestones
An AI use policy draft
A presentation to the SCAiL cohort

slides.title: What You Walk Away With
bullets: An AI implementation plan ready for your board
A pitch deck for an AI-enabled venture or program
A grant prospect list and draft LOI
A network of SC AI-literate leaders
A SCAiL Leadership Academy credential

sc-8.title: Train the Trainer: AI Education Certification

slides.title: Twelve Weeks to Certified
items: Module 2: Teaching AI to non-technical audiences
Module 6: Practicum — teach a real workshop

slides.text: Every community in South Carolina deserves a SCAiL-certified educator within 30 minutes of home. That's the goal. You're how we get there.

slides.title: What Every Educator Must Know
bullets: How large language models actually work, in plain English
What 'training data' is and why it matters
Why AI hallucinates — and how to spot it
The difference between generative and predictive AI
Where AI is heading in the next 2 years

slides.title: Translate, Don't Lecture
bullets: Replace every jargon word with a plain-English version
Use stories before stats
Use familiar examples — not Silicon Valley ones
Anchor every concept in something the learner already knows
If they look confused, you went too fast
slides.note: This is the most important skill in this entire program. Spend extra time.

slides.title: The Three-Layer Explanation
bullets: Layer 1: A 10-second explanation a child could repeat
Layer 2: A 1-minute explanation a curious adult would enjoy
Layer 3: A 5-minute explanation for someone who wants depth
Always start at Layer 1
Only go deeper when asked

slides.title: Building a Workshop From Scratch
bullets: Start with the outcome — what should learners be able to DO?
Work backwards from outcomes to activities
Build in hands-on practice every 15 minutes
Plan for technology failures — always have an offline backup
End with a clear next step for every learner

slides.title: Holding the Room
bullets: Read the room every 5 minutes — adjust as needed
Use silence — wait at least 7 seconds for answers
Repeat questions back so the whole room can hear
Welcome 'wrong' answers — they teach the room more than right ones
Always end with energy, not exhaustion

slides.title: Hands-On: Teach a 3-Minute Concept
steps: Pair up with another educator-in-training
Each of you picks one AI concept to teach
Take turns teaching it in 3 minutes, no more
Give each other one piece of specific feedback
Note what worked — that's what you'll use in your practicum

slides.title: Did They Actually Learn?
bullets: Use 'show me' over 'tell me' — learners demonstrate, not recite
Pre and post surveys to measure confidence shifts
One-month follow-up: did they actually use AI?
Story collection — testimonials are gold for funders
Refine your curriculum based on real outcomes

slides.title: Teach a Real Workshop
bullets: Pick one SCAiL course to deliver in your community
Co-teach with a SCAiL mentor your first time
Lead solo your second time
Collect feedback from at least 5 participants
Reflect on what you'd change — and do it

slides.title: What Certification Means
bullets: You can deliver any SCAiL workshop independently
You can co-design new curriculum with the SCAiL team
You earn the SCAiL-Certified AI Educator credential
You join a statewide network of certified educators
You can earn stipends for delivering workshops

slides.title: Your Educator Toolkit
bullets: Full facilitator guides for every SCAiL course
Editable slide decks (these — the ones you're holding now)
Handout templates and assessment rubrics
Access to the SCAiL trainer Slack
Ongoing professional development sessions

slides.title: What You Walk Away With
bullets: SCAiL-Certified AI Educator credential
A complete teaching toolkit for 8 SCAiL courses
Real practicum experience teaching in your community
A statewide network of fellow certified educators
The ability to bring AI literacy to anyone, anywhere in SC
